macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks close higher after softer July CPI and strong AI earnings
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.26%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.74%, and the Dow was little changed after July core CPI came in at 2.5% year over year, supporting expectations for easier Fed policy. The rally was led by AI and chip shares after better-than-expected earnings from CoreWeave and Super Micro.

items.title: Inflation moderates in July, keeping Fed rate-cut expectations in focus
items.summary: The Labor Department reported that U.S. CPI rose 0.1% in July and 3.4% year over year, while core inflation increased 2.5% annually. Markets viewed the softer reading as evidence that inflation is cooling, though it remains above the Fed’s 2% target.

items.title: Stock futures edge higher ahead of inflation data
items.summary: U.S. stock futures moved higher before the inflation release, with sentiment helped by upbeat earnings from several technology companies. The report framed the market as waiting for fresh clues on the outlook for interest rates.

items.title: Markets price lower odds of a Fed hike after cooler CPI
items.summary: Following the CPI report, markets reduced the implied probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the next FOMC meeting to 40% from 51% the prior day. Treasury yields were little changed as investors recalibrated the policy outlook.

items.title: Indian shares slip as inflation rises and Tata group stocks fall
items.summary: India’s Sensex fell about 0.2% and the Nifty closed below 24,450 after retail inflation rose to 4.45% in July and Tata Sons chairman N. Chandrasekaran resigned, pressuring Tata-related stocks. Rising oil prices and a weaker rupee also weighed on sentiment.

items.title: Sensex and Nifty finish lower in thin risk sentiment
items.summary: Provisional closing data showed the Sensex down 187.90 points to 77,966.35 and the Nifty down 35.75 points to 24,435.95. The broader market also weakened as investors awaited U.S. inflation data and watched global yields.

items.title: Gold holds near record highs, oil remains above $84 ahead of U.S. CPI
items.summary: Commodity markets stayed cautious before the inflation report, with gold near $4,400 an ounce and WTI crude holding above $84. The move reflected investor uncertainty over the Fed path and geopolitics.

items.title: Nifty and Sensex open weak as oil and inflation pressure sentiment
items.summary: Market commentary highlighted that higher oil prices, inflation concerns, and global caution kept Asian equities mixed and U.S. futures slightly positive ahead of the CPI release. The note also pointed to cautious positioning in the run-up to U.S. data.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum hold near recent ranges as crypto market stays flat
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $63.7K and Ethereum near $1.89K over the past 24 hours, while the total crypto market cap remained roughly flat around $2.19T. XRP and Solana saw mixed performance, with XRP weaker and Solana slightly higher.

items.title: SEC may soon unveil a tokenized stock trading exemption
items.summary: Market watchers reported that the SEC could unveil a tokenized stock trading exemption as soon as Friday, a development that would be a notable regulatory step for tokenized assets and crypto-linked trading products. The same recap also highlighted Kalshi's July revenue run rate topping $4 billion, reflecting continued growth in digital-asset-adjacent trading activity.

items.title: Harmony exploit mints billions of ONE tokens and sends price tumbling
items.summary: Harmony confirmed a protocol exploit that allowed an attacker to mint about 4 billion ONE tokens, equal to roughly 26% of circulating supply. Around 2.8 billion tokens were quickly sent to exchanges, and ONE fell as much as 40% to a record low.

items.title: Bitcoin slips below $64,000 as traders await U.S. inflation data
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $63.3K to $63.7K as markets stayed cautious ahead of inflation data, with broader crypto sentiment soft and prices mostly rangebound. Ethereum and several large-cap altcoins were mixed, while BNB briefly reached a two-month high before easing.

items.title: Crypto market declines slightly after in-line U.S. CPI reading
items.summary: U.S. inflation data that matched expectations coincided with a mild drop in crypto market capitalization, while Bitcoin slipped about 0.6% and Ethereum held slightly higher. The report said U.S.-listed Bitcoin spot ETF inflows helped limit losses and liquidations reached roughly $210 million over 24 hours.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $64,000 as ETF inflows continue
items.summary: Bitcoin remained around $63.5K to $63.7K, down about 0.6% over 24 hours, despite renewed ETF inflows and broader gains in risk assets earlier in the week. The report also noted Wells Fargo's plan to launch tokenized deposits this fall, expanding corporate blockchain-based payments.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google’s Gemini app reaches 1 billion users as the company reshuffles AI leadership
items.summary: Google said its Gemini app has grown to 1 billion users, while Reuters reported that Sergey Brin has urged staff to focus on Gemini and that Google recently overhauled DeepMind leadership to speed up its AI push.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT desktop app for Linux
items.summary: OpenAI released a Linux desktop app for ChatGPT, expanding access to the company’s flagship product beyond Windows and macOS.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly completed a $7 billion employee tender offer
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that OpenAI finished a large employee tender offer, a sign of continuing investor demand for the company despite ongoing scrutiny around valuation and competition.

items.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings raises $2 billion for enterprise AI
items.summary: Thrive Holdings secured a $2 billion raise to build and scale enterprise-focused AI businesses, underscoring continued investor interest in applied AI software.

items.title: Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its AI models
items.summary: Anthropic announced it will add invisible watermarking to text from its models, a move aimed at making AI-generated content easier to identify and trace.

items.title: OpenAI pauses work on a model over serious cybersecurity risks
items.summary: PCMag reported that OpenAI halted work on an unreleased model, called Astra, after it showed signs it could autonomously carry out cyberattacks.

items.title: Chinese hackers used open-source AI agents in a near-autonomous attack
items.summary: PCMag reported that attackers used open-source AI agents to break into 85 government accounts and steal personal records in roughly four days, highlighting the growing abuse of AI tools in cybercrime.

items.title: AI infrastructure stocks surge after strong CoreWeave and Supermicro earnings
items.summary: Markets rallied on stronger-than-expected results from CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer, reinforcing investor enthusiasm for AI infrastructure, data-center buildout, and related hardware demand.

items.title: CoreWeave shares jump after revenue doubles from a year earlier
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that CoreWeave shares rose after the company said revenue had doubled year over year, adding to signs of strong demand for AI compute.

items.title: Anthropic model reportedly made progress on a major math problem
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that an unreleased Anthropic model showed progress on one of mathematics’ biggest unsolved problems, suggesting continued frontier-model gains in reasoning and scientific problem-solving.

items.title: Spotify will label AI persona profiles and exclude them from recommendations
items.summary: Spotify announced that it will flag AI-generated persona profiles and remove their music from recommendations, reflecting a broader industry effort to manage synthetic media.

items.title: Made by Google 2026 featured major Gemini integrations and new Pixel hardware
items.summary: TechCrunch said Google’s latest event introduced new Pixel devices alongside a wide set of Gemini features, showing that consumer AI remains central to the company’s product strategy.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Wall Street firms pledge more than $500 billion to Nvidia-linked AI infrastructure
items.summary: Major financial firms are committing over $500 billion to fund data centers and infrastructure tied to Nvidia-powered AI projects, underscoring continued heavy capital spending across the tech sector. The move is one of the biggest recent industry-financing developments affecting semiconductor and cloud infrastructure demand.

items.title: Spotify to label AI-generated artists and remove them from recommendations
items.summary: Spotify is adding a label for AI-generated artists starting in mid-September and will exclude them from recommendations. The change is one of the clearest recent platform policy shifts around synthetic media in music.

items.title: Meta fined $567 million in major child safety ruling
items.summary: Meta has been hit with a $567 million fine in what is described as the largest child-safety ruling against a social media company. The decision adds to regulatory pressure on large consumer-tech platforms.

items.title: Google finally launches its own Bluetooth tracker, Pixel Tag
items.summary: Google has launched Pixel Tag, its first Bluetooth tracker, expanding its hardware lineup into a category long dominated by rival accessories. The launch is notable as a consumer-product move rather than an AI announcement.

items.title: Nvidia stock swings as third-party capital tops $500 billion for AI projects
items.summary: Nvidia shares moved sharply after reports that more than $500 billion in outside capital has been lined up for AI infrastructure spending. The reaction highlights how closely the semiconductor market is tied to cloud and data-center investment plans.

items.title: Google’s chief scientist departs to start new startup
items.summary: Google’s current chief scientist is leaving the company to found a new startup with three former Google veterans. The departure is another significant personnel shift inside the tech industry.

items.title: Etsy to cut about 12% of its global workforce
items.summary: Etsy is reducing its global workforce by roughly 12%, reflecting continued cost-cutting and restructuring among major tech platforms. The move is one of the more significant company-news items in the broader tech sector.

items.title: Tech stocks drive market gains as Nasdaq outperforms
items.summary: Technology names again led market performance, with the Nasdaq rising while the Dow lagged. The trading pattern points to continued investor concentration in large tech stocks.
